standard_prerequisites.name: The pullback-perfect lemma: perfection is preserved by base change and can be pulled back
The cutting lemma for a complex vanishing at a prime, and tor-amplitude of the upper truncation
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the direct sum decomposition whose lower half must be shown to vanish.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pseudo-coherence giving finite cohomology, and Nakayama's lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the pair that makes the contradiction argument close.

core_obligations: Deduce (1) => (2) from the pullback-perfect lemma (proof line 20089).
Establish (2) => (3) immediately, and (3) => (2) by applying the pullback-perfect lemma to R_m -> R_p, using that every prime p is contained in a maximal ideal m (proof lines 20090-20093).
Apply the pullback-perfect lemma to the residue maps R_p -> kappa(p) and R_m -> kappa(m) to get (2) => (4) and (3) => (5) (proof lines 20094-20097).

In the local case with residue field kappa, assume H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa) = 0 for i < a and invoke the cutting lemma with i = a - 1 to write K^bullet = tau_{<= a-1}K^bullet oplus tau_{>= a}K^bullet in D(R), with tau_{>= a} perfect of tor-amplitude in [a, infinity] (proof lines 20100-20109).

Show tau_{<= a-1}K^bullet is zero by contradiction: take the largest index i with M = H^i(tau_{<= a-1}K^bullet) nonzero, use pseudo-coherence to see M is a finite R-module, apply Nakayama to get M tensor_R kappa nonzero, and conclude that H^i(tau_{<= a-1}K^bullet tensor^L kappa) = H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa) is nonzero, contradicting the hypothesis (proof lines 20110-20122).
Conclude (4) => (2) and (5) => (3), completing the first part of the lemma (proof lines 20103-20105).

Assuming the equivalent conditions (2) to (5) and that K^bullet is bounded below with H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i < a, pick a maximal ideal m and produce f not in m with K^bullet tensor^L R_f perfect, citing the gluing lemma, quasi-compactness and the lift lemma, which gives all conditions equivalent (proof lines 20125-20132).
difficulty_reason: The lemma lists five conditions on a pseudo-coherent complex K^bullet over a ring R: that it be perfect; that its localization at every prime be perfect; the same at every maximal ideal; the vanishing of H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa(p)) for all i much smaller than 0 at every prime; and the same at every maximal ideal; it asserts the implications (1) => (2) <=> (3) <=> (4) <=> (5), with all conditions equivalent when K^bullet is bounded below (source lines 20063-20086). The proof has real content beyond the formal implications. The localization implications come from applying the pullback-perfect lemma to the appropriate maps of local rings and residue fields, and the passage from primes to maximal ideals uses that every prime lies in a maximal ideal and then pulls back along R_m -> R_p (proof lines 20089-20097). The substantive direction is that (4) implies (2) and (5) implies (3): in the local case with vanishing below degree a, the proof invokes the cutting lemma at i = a - 1 to split K^bullet as the direct sum of tau_{<= a-1} and tau_{>= a} with the upper part perfect, and then shows the lower part vanishes by a contradiction: if not, the largest nonzero cohomology module M is finite by pseudo-coherence, so by Nakayama M tensor_R kappa is nonzero, which makes H^i((tau_{<= a-1}K^bullet) tensor^L kappa) = H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa) nonzero, contradicting the hypothesis (proof lines 20100-20122). The bounded below case is then finished by producing, at any given maximal ideal, an f outside it with K^bullet tensor R_f perfect, using the gluing and lift lemmas together with quasi-compactness (proof lines 20125-20132). The non-routine steps are the Nakayama contradiction and the final local-to-global promotion.
